outline.title: Average speed
keyPoints: Term: average speed
Definition: total distance travelled divided by total time taken
Used to compare journeys of different lengths
Micro-example: 120 km in 2 h is 60 km/h

outline.title: The speed formula
keyPoints: Rule: speed = distance ÷ time
Distance and time must use matching units
Applies to the whole journey, including stops
Exception: it does not give the speed at one instant

outline.title: Solving a two-part journey
keyPoints: Problem: 60 km in 1 h, then 90 km in 2 h — find the average speed
Step 1: add distances (150 km) — the rule needs TOTAL distance
Step 2: add times (3 h) — the rule needs TOTAL time
Step 3: divide 150 ÷ 3 = 50 km/h
Result: 50 km/h; takeaway: never average the two speeds
